meta.triageRationale: Small bugfix (ISSUE-8d7b4704660a5866): the native VS Code id of the convert escalation role is a dotted child of another native id.

body.focus: Fix the VS Code setting for the convert escalation tier (ISSUE-8d7b4704660a5866): give models.tasks.tools.convert.escalate a native setting id that is not a dotted child of another setting id (insrc.models.tasks.tools.convertEscalate), map it back to the unchanged catalog path in vscode-plugin/src/config/key-map.ts and scripts/sync-manifest-catalog.mjs, regenerate vscode-plugin/package.json, move an existing user value from the old id once at activation in vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts, and add a test that no native setting id is a dotted prefix of another.
body.summary: vscode-plugin/src/config/key-map.ts gains nativeRoleKey: a role whose id extends another role's id with a dot joins the rest onto the parent in camel case, so tools.convert.escalate gets the native id insrc.models.tasks.tools.convertEscalate; every other role keeps insrc.models.tasks.<roleId>. buildPerRoleKeyMap uses it and the catalog path models.tasks.tools.convert.escalate is unchanged; vscode-plugin/package.json declares the renamed setting. New src/config/legacy-keys.ts: migrateLegacyKeys moves a valid tier typed under the old id to the new id once, after the activation pull (src/extension.ts), only when the new id still shows its default, and clears the old id best effort (VS Code refuses to write an unregistered setting). Tests: per-role.test.ts (derivation, the escalation role's mapping, and that no declared or mapped native id is a dotted prefix of another; it fails with the old key restored) and legacy-keys.test.ts (move, no-overwrite, invalid and failing deps). scripts/sync-manifest-catalog.mjs needed no change: it leaves the per-role keys alone and the taxonomy-coverage test guards them. Not checked: behaviour inside a running VS Code. repo-config.test.ts has two failures that exist without this change (it hardcodes 14 critical and 20 peripheral roles).
